footnotes: p. 11 n. 1 (on 'à', l. 11): An interesting variant of this passage occurs on the leather roll, British Museum No. 10,473; it runs :— [prints the variant in hieroglyphs, 2 rows]

p. 12 n. 1 (on 'śenit', l. 13): In the papyrus of Hunefer (British Museum No. 9901) this chapter ends with the words, "the Shenit, in the presence of the great god, lord of Amenta," but in several others, all of a later date, the chapter has here the words :— [2 interlinear rows: śenit àriu reθ em āḥāu nefer-en-n nefer-en setem āu àb en ut'ā t'eṭu, 'the Shenit who make men and women to be in stability. Pleasant [is it] for us pleasant [is it] to hear gladness of heart at the weighing of words.'] Here follows the petition, "let not lies be spoken ([hieroglyphs] equals [hieroglyph]) against me near the great god, in the presence of the great god, lord of Amenta," and the chapter ends with, [māk θenθ - k un - θà em maāχeru] "Verily how great wilt thou be rising up in triumph!"
p. 12 n. 2 (on 'āḥāu - s', Anubis legend): Compare the legend in the papyrus of Ànhai (British Museum No. 10,472) :— [prints it in hieroglyphs, 2 rows]
p. 15 n. 1 (on 'χennu', in the Appendix - outside this reader's range): Compare [hieroglyphs], Naville, Todtenbuch, Bd. II., Bl. 99.

p. 15 n. 2 (on 'Teḥuti', l. 16): In British Museum papyrus No. 9901, the speech of Thoth reads :— [2 interlinear rows: māk - à ḥer metru ren en Àusàr suten ān Hunefer àu àb - f pert ḥer māχa bu qem - nef t'ai, 'Verily I am justifying the name of Osiris the royal scribe Hunefer. His heart hath come forth upon the Scale, not hath he been found an evil doer.']
p. 16 n. 1 (on 'χemennu', l. 26): The variants are [hieroglyphs: several variant writings of the name].

p. 18 n. 1 (on Àusàr, Pl. IV l. 3): "In British Museum papyrus No. 9901, the speech of Horus reads :—" followed by a parallel text in hieroglyphs (3 rows) with transliteration (t'et àn Ḥeru net' tef - f uā menχ en Un-nefer mākuà ḥer bes - nek Àusàr Hu-nefer àu - f sàp mā māχa àu pa teχ hui er àuset-f) and translation: "Saith Horus the avenger of his father, heir veritable of Un-nefer: I am come to lead to thee Osiris Hu-nefer. He hath been judged in the scales, the weight of the balance resteth (?) upon its place."
layoutNote: Plate III ll. 1–30 (pp. 11–12, 15–17) and Plate IV ll. 1–10 (pp. 17–19). The words above the head of Anubis (p. 12) are a vignette legend, given line 15 and flagged "legend"; a hatched lacuna (about one group, "......") stands after maāt at the start of its second row (see "gaps"). Rubric (overlined) at the head of each speech. On p. 16 l. 26 Budge prints "...." under a sign he does not read (coded V25 approx + I9). On p. 18 l. 5 the overlined cobra-and-hand group has no transliteration or English under it (budge "(none printed)"). Square brackets in the hieroglyph line: the A1 of mut - à and χeperu - [à] (p. 11) and the N35 Z2 of Ani (p. 18 l. 5), flagged restored.
